subject: general
question: The Modern Periodic Table based on ________ of the elements.
solution:
The correct answer is **Atomic Number**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number** is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The Modern Periodic Table is arranged in order of increasing **atomic number**.
 
• This arrangement resolves anomalies present in Mendeleev's periodic table, which was based on atomic mass.
 
• Elements with similar properties recur at regular intervals or periods when arranged by increasing **atomic number**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1: Valency
 Valency is the combining capacity of an element, but it does not determine the arrangement in the periodic table.
 
 

 Option 2: Equivalent Weight
 Equivalent weight is the mass of an element that combines with or displaces 1.008 parts by mass of hydrogen. It is not used for the modern arrangement.
 
 

 Option 3: Atomic Number
 Atomic number is the basis for the modern periodic table. It represents the number of protons in an atom's nucleus.
 
 

 Option 4: Atomic Mass
 Atomic mass was used in Mendeleev's periodic table but led to some inconsistencies which were resolved by using atomic number.
